caption: Someone wrote “DO NOT USE” on it in biro. No need to actually disconnect it then….🙄
A switch hanging out of the wall on a choc block, red and black wiring dating it nicely. At least they painted around it neatly….🙄
Hunting for the cable by cutting holes in the ceiling until one of them finds it….🙄
Unsheathed singles poking out of the plaster straight into an open connection box, plaster dust and all….😬
A live cable buried in a child’s bedroom wall with nothing protecting it. The volt stick lit up like the big top above it….😬
Cracked clean through and scorched black around the pin. Still screwed to the wall, still being used….😱
Blue insulating tape, the professional’s choice for joining a cable inside a metal box….🙄
An outdoor junction box hanging open with bare copper on show. The spiders had clearly moved in years ago….😬
Bare strands hanging out of the terminal and a screw so corroded it had given up completely. All hidden neatly out of sight….🙄
The supply cable fed in through a bare hole with no gland and nothing to hold it, resting on the edge of the plastic enclosure….😬
The decorator painted straight over the storage heater controls. Dial, buttons, display and all….🙄
A ceiling rose used as a joint box, lying loose in the floor void. Old colours and new all in together….😬
The sheath stripped back where the cable crosses the joist, leaving the earth on show in the loft….😬
Don’t worry about connecting those live cables into your metal socket….😬😱
Don’t worry about earthing the steel wired armoured cable. Just lash it in and hope for the best! 🙄😬
Excellent use of of push fit plumbing elbow joint….🙄
They may have used a slightly too big drill bit for this earthing. Never mind, leaving a huge whole was nice of them. The weather and mice really appreciate it….🙄
